title: UP BOARD CLASS 6 — Science | Heat
description: Subject-wise test on Heat (Science) for UP BOARD CLASS 6. 10Q.
subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Heat is a form of:
questions.explanation: Heat is defined as a form of energy that flows from a hotter body to a colder body.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: The standard unit commonly used to measure temperature is:
questions.explanation: Temperature is typically measured in degrees Celsius (°C) in many parts of the world, including for common use and in scientific contexts at this level.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Which of the following materials is a good conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal and metals are generally good conductors of heat, meaning they allow heat to pass through them easily. Wood, plastic, and glass are poor conductors (insulators).
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor conductor of heat (an insulator)?
questions.explanation: Air is a very poor conductor of heat because its molecules are far apart and do not transfer heat efficiently through conduction. Iron, aluminium, and silver are all metals and good conductors.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Woolen clothes keep us warm during winter because:

options.text: They trap air, which is a poor conductor of heat.

questions.explanation: Woolen fibres trap a lot of air in their spaces. This trapped air acts as an insulator, preventing the heat from our body from escaping into the cold surroundings.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: When water is heated in a pot on a stove, the heat transfer primarily occurs through which mode within the water?
questions.explanation: Convection is the primary mode of heat transfer in liquids and gases. The heated water at the bottom becomes less dense and rises, while cooler, denser water from the top sinks to be heated, creating a convection current.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Why are dark-coloured clothes preferred during winter?
questions.explanation: Dark surfaces absorb more heat radiation from the sun and the surroundings compared to light surfaces, which reflect more heat. This helps to keep the wearer warmer in winter.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: The ultimate natural source of heat energy for the Earth is:
questions.explanation: The Sun is the primary natural source of heat and light energy for Earth, driving most of its weather patterns and supporting life.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** Metals like iron and copper are used to make cooking utensils. **Reason (R):** Metals are good conductors of heat.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.explanation: Metals are indeed used for cooking utensils because their property of being good conductors of heat allows them to quickly transfer heat from the stove to the food, which is exactly why they are chosen. Thus, the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Imagine you are making tea. The kettle is made of stainless steel, and its handle is covered with a thick plastic. Why is this specific design chosen?

options.text: Both stainless steel and plastic are good conductors of heat.
Stainless steel is a good conductor of heat, while plastic is a poor conductor (insulator).
Stainless steel is a poor conductor of heat, while plastic is a good conductor.
Both stainless steel and plastic are poor conductors of heat.

questions.explanation: Stainless steel is a metal, making it a good conductor to quickly heat the water inside. Plastic, on the other hand, is a poor conductor (an insulator), which prevents the heat from the hot kettle body from reaching your hand, protecting you from burns.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: The measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of an object is called its:

options.explanation: Energy is the capacity to do work, not a measure of hotness or coldness.
Temperature is the standard scientific measure that indicates how hot or cold an object is relative to a standard value.
Pressure is the force applied perpendicular to the surface of an object per unit area.
Volume is the amount of space an object occupies.

questions.explanation: Temperature is the standard scientific measure that indicates how hot or cold an object is relative to a standard value.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Which of the following materials is a good conductor of heat?

options.explanation: Wood is an insulator and a poor conductor of heat.
Plastic is an insulator and a poor conductor of heat.
Metals like copper allow heat to pass through them easily, making them good conductors of heat.
Rubber is an insulator and a poor conductor of heat.

questions.explanation: Metals like copper allow heat to pass through them easily, making them good conductors of heat, whereas wood, plastic, and rubber are insulators.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: What is the normal temperature of a healthy human body on the Celsius scale?

options.explanation: 32°C is below the normal human body temperature.
The average normal temperature of a healthy human body is 37°C.
42°C indicates a high fever, not normal body temperature.
98.6 is the normal body temperature in Fahrenheit, not Celsius.

questions.explanation: The average normal temperature of a healthy human body is 37°C (or 98.6°F).
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth primarily through which process of heat transfer?

options.explanation: Conduction requires direct contact between particles and a material medium.
Convection requires the movement of fluids (liquids or gases) and cannot occur in a vacuum.
Radiation does not require any material medium for the transfer of heat, allowing heat energy from the Sun to travel through the vacuum of space to reach the Earth.
Absorption is the process of taking in energy, not a mode of heat transfer across space.

questions.explanation: Radiation does not require any material medium for the transfer of heat, allowing heat energy from the Sun to travel through the vacuum of space to reach the Earth.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Why are the handles of metallic cooking pans usually covered with plastic or wood?

options.text: Plastic and wood are poor conductors of heat, preventing burns.
options.explanation: Wood and plastic are insulators (poor conductors of heat), so heat from the metallic pan is not transferred to our hands, keeping the handle safe to touch.

options.text: Plastic and wood make the pan look decorative.
options.explanation: While they may look decorative, the primary reason is safety.

options.text: Plastic and wood absorb heat rapidly to cook food faster.
options.explanation: Plastic and wood are insulators and do not absorb heat rapidly to aid cooking.

options.text: Plastic and wood are heavy and balance the weight of the pan.
options.explanation: Plastic and wood are generally lightweight and not used for balancing weight.

questions.explanation: Wood and plastic are insulators (poor conductors of heat), so heat from the metallic pan is not transferred to our hands, keeping the handle safe to touch.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: What is the normal temperature of a healthy human body on the Celsius scale?

options.explanation: 35°C is slightly below the normal body temperature.
37°C is the standard normal body temperature for a healthy human.
98.6 is the normal body temperature in Fahrenheit, not Celsius. 98.6°C would be lethal.
100°C is the boiling point of water and is far too hot for a human body.

questions.explanation: The normal temperature of a healthy human body is 37°C (which is equivalent to 98.6°F).
questions.hint: Think about the standard body temperature taught in science classes.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: The device used to measure the degree of hotness or coldness of an object is called a:

options.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
A speedometer measures the speed of a vehicle.
A thermometer is used to measure temperature.
An anemometer measures wind speed.

questions.explanation: A thermometer is an instrument specifically designed to measure temperature (the degree of hotness or coldness of an object).
questions.hint: The word starts with 'Th' and ends with 'meter'.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Which of the following materials is a good conductor of heat?

options.explanation: Dry wood is an insulator and a poor conductor of heat.
Plastic is an insulator and a poor conductor of heat.
Copper is a metal and a very good conductor of heat.
Rubber is an insulator and a poor conductor of heat.

questions.explanation: Metals like copper readily allow heat to pass through them, making them good conductors of heat. Wood, plastic, and rubber are insulators.
questions.hint: Metals are generally good conductors, while non-metals like wood and plastic are insulators.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: What is the normal measuring range of a clinical thermometer used to check body temperature?

options.explanation: This is the range of a laboratory thermometer, not a clinical one.
This range covers the possible variations in human body temperature.
This range is too wide and includes temperatures not relevant to human body measurement.
This range is too broad and does not specifically target the narrow range of human body temperature.

questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer is designed only to measure human body temperature, which rarely falls below 35°C or rises above 42°C. Hence, its range is 35°C to 42°C.
questions.hint: Consider the typical range of human body temperatures, from slightly low to dangerously high.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Cooking utensils are usually made of metals, but their handles are made of wood or plastic. Why?

options.text: Wood and plastic look more attractive than metals
options.explanation: Aesthetics are not the primary reason for using wood or plastic for handles.

options.text: Wood and plastic are poor conductors of heat and do not get hot easily
options.explanation: Wood and plastic are insulators, which prevents heat from the metal utensil from reaching the hand.

options.text: Wood and plastic make the utensil much heavier and stable
options.explanation: Wood and plastic are generally lighter than metals, so they do not make the utensil heavier.

options.text: Metals melt quickly when touched by hand
options.explanation: Metals do not melt when touched by hand; they conduct heat, which can cause burns.

questions.explanation: Wood and plastic are insulators (poor conductors of heat). They prevent the heat from the hot utensil from transferring to our hands, allowing us to hold them safely.
questions.hint: Think about the property of wood and plastic that prevents heat transfer.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: A metal spoon is placed inside a bowl of hot soup. After a few minutes, the other end of the spoon becomes hot. By which process has heat traveled through the spoon?

options.explanation: Radiation does not require a medium and travels in straight lines, typically through space or air, not through the solid structure of a spoon.
Convection occurs in fluids (liquids and gases) due to the movement of particles, not in solids like a metal spoon.
Conduction is the transfer of heat through direct contact within a solid material, which is how heat travels through the spoon.
Evaporation is a phase change from liquid to gas, not a mode of heat transfer through a solid.

questions.explanation: Conduction is the process of heat transfer in solids where heat passes from the hotter end to the colder end from particle to particle without the actual movement of the particles themselves.
questions.hint: Think about how heat moves through solid objects.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Why does wearing two thin sweaters keep a person warmer than wearing a single thick sweater of the same total thickness?

options.text: Two thin sweaters are heavier than one thick sweater
options.explanation: Weight is not the primary factor in insulation; the trapping of air is the key mechanism.

options.text: Air is trapped between the two layers of sweaters, which acts as an insulator
options.explanation: The trapped air acts as an insulator because air is a poor conductor of heat, reducing heat loss from the body.

options.text: Two sweaters generate extra heat on their own
options.explanation: Clothing does not generate heat; it only helps retain the body's heat.

options.text: Wool in thin sweaters allows body coldness to escape outside
options.explanation: This statement is scientifically incorrect; coldness does not escape, heat is retained.

questions.explanation: Air is a poor conductor of heat. The layer of air trapped between the two thin sweaters prevents the flow of heat from our body to the cold surroundings, keeping us warmer.
questions.hint: Consider the role of air trapped between layers of clothing.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: What is the specific function of the 'kink' (constriction) present in the capillary tube of a clinical thermometer?

options.text: It increases the speed at which mercury expands
options.explanation: The kink does not affect the speed of expansion; it affects the movement of mercury after heating.

options.text: It prevents the mercury level from falling on its own before reading the temperature
options.explanation: The kink breaks the mercury column when it cools, preventing it from returning to the bulb so the reading can be taken outside the body.

options.text: It helps the thermometer to measure temperatures above 100°C
options.explanation: Clinical thermometers are designed for body temperature (35°C-42°C), not high temperatures.

options.text: It prevents the glass tube from breaking under high heat
options.explanation: The kink is for functional accuracy, not structural integrity against heat.

questions.explanation: The kink prevents the mercury thread from flowing back into the bulb when the thermometer is removed from the patient's mouth or armpit, allowing an accurate reading to be taken.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the mercury when the thermometer is removed from the body.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): We feel warm when we sit in front of an electric room heater without touching it.
Reason (R): Heat from the room heater reaches us directly by radiation, which does not require any material medium.
Choose the correct option:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.explanation: We feel warmth without contact because heat travels via radiation, which does not need a medium, correctly explaining the assertion.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
options.explanation: The reason is indeed the correct explanation for why we feel heat without touching the heater.
The reason is true; radiation does not require a medium.
The assertion is true; we do feel warm in front of a heater.

questions.explanation: Heat transfer by radiation does not require any physical medium. The heat from a room heater travels across the space directly to our body via radiation, making both the assertion and reason correct.
questions.hint: Evaluate if both statements are true and if the reason explains the assertion.
questions.subject: upbo6-science

questions.question: Case Study: Ramesh took two identical tin cans, labeled 'X' and 'Y'. He painted the outer surface of can 'X' black and can 'Y' white. He filled both cans with equal amounts of water at 25°C and kept them under direct sunlight for two hours. What will Ramesh observe after two hours, and what is the scientific reason?

options.text: Water in can Y is hotter because white surfaces reflect heat directly into the water.
options.explanation: White surfaces reflect heat rather than absorbing it, so the water in can Y will be cooler.

options.text: Water in can X is hotter because dark-colored surfaces absorb more heat radiation than light-colored surfaces.
options.explanation: Black surfaces absorb more heat radiation, leading to a higher temperature in can X.

options.text: Water in both cans will remain at 25°C because sunlight does not heat water in metal cans.
options.explanation: Sunlight does heat water in metal cans, especially when the can absorbs the radiation.

options.text: Water in can Y is hotter because light-colored surfaces absorb radiation faster than dark surfaces.
options.explanation: Light-colored surfaces absorb less radiation than dark surfaces.

questions.explanation: Dark or black surfaces are much better absorbers of heat radiation than light or white surfaces. Therefore, can X absorbs more heat from the sun, raising the temperature of its water higher than that in can Y.
questions.hint: Consider how different colors interact with sunlight.
questions.subject: upbo6-science
